terms.grammar: adverb and conjunction, with adjectives and adverbs
evidence: Catull. 3.6–7: suamque nōrat ipsam tam bene quam puella mātrem
terms.comment: Tam goes with the adjective or adverb, quam introduces the other term, in the same case: tam bene quam puella.

terms.gloss: as big as, as much as, as many as
terms.grammar: correlative pronouns and adverbs: size, amount and number
evidence: Cic. Fam. 16.2.1: quantum mē dīligis, tantum fac ut valeās
terms.comment: For size tantus … quantus, for amount tantum … quantum, for number tot … quot; the quantus-clause may come first.

terms.grammar: quam with a superlative adjective or adverb
evidence: Plin. Ep. 6.7.3: tū tamen quam frequentissimē scrībe
Cato Agr. 66: quam mundissimē pūrissimēque fīat
terms.comment: Quam prīmum, as soon as possible; quam plūrimī, as many as possible.

phrases.latin: nam mellītus erat suamque nōrat ipsam tam bene quam puella mātrem
phrases.english: for he was sweet as honey, and knew his mistress as well as a little girl knows her mother

phrases.latin: quantum mē dīligis, tantum fac ut valeās
phrases.english: as much as you love me, so much see that you get well
all the same, do write as often as you can
let it be done as cleanly and purely as possible

phrases.latin: aut quam sīdera multa, cum tacet nox
phrases.english: or as many as the stars, when the night is silent
